title: Award Letter Decoder
creator: Beth Kullberg
subject: College Admissions
description: Translate any financial aid award letter into standard numbers: sort each line into free, earned, or borrowed money, then see the real net price and out-of-pocket cost.

learningObjectives: Students will classify each line of an award letter as free, earned, or borrowed money and calculate the offer's net price and out-of-pocket cost, ignoring misleading letter totals.

controls: Lakeshore, College C, Hillcrest, and Enter my own buttons
Accept work-study and accept student loans checkboxes
Own-letter line name, amount, type, Add line, and Remove last controls

keyQuestions: Why isn't a Parent PLUS loan financial aid?
What is the difference between net price and out-of-pocket cost?
What should you do when a letter leaves out the cost of attendance?
commonMisconceptions: The letter's total aid is the discount.
Loans listed as awards are free money.
assessmentOpportunities: Students sort a new award letter correctly and calculate its net price and out-of-pocket cost.
